title: Write a weather line
prompt: `city` is a supplied string and `temp` is a supplied whole number. Declare a string named `label` in the form `"Oslo: 3 degrees"`: the city, a colon and a space, the number, a space, then the word degrees. Build it from the supplied values so it works for every case.
hints: Which parts of the label change from case to case, and which stay the same?
An interpolated string starts with $ before the opening quote.
Inside the $ string, put city and temp in braces, and type the colon, the spaces and the word degrees as plain text.
checkLabels: label must be the city, a colon and a space, the temperature, then the word degrees.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Copies the worked example as fixed text.
Leaves off the $, so the braces stay as ordinary text.

feedback: Compare your label with the expected text one character at a time. Check the $ before the quote and the spaces around the number.
